about: Judgments behind scripts/skills-inventory.py: the useful-skill definition, a group per skill, a keep/merge/remove verdict per copy (matched by name and a path fragment), and the harness notes that restate a skill. Facts such as hashes, links and usage come from the scan, never from this file.
definition: A useful skill is one that real sessions load and act on, and it passes five tests. 1. Transcripts from the last 30 days show agents reading its SKILL.md, calling its Python module or CLI, or invoking it through Claude Code's Skill tool; being listed in the system prompt does not count. 2. Its text changes what an agent does: it carries a procedure, an API, paths or checks a model would get wrong without it. 3. It holds more than one rule (c99); a single rule belongs in AGENTS.md or the area's existing skill. 4. It exists once per box and loads one way; an upstream skill stays as upstream ships it (c226), with no unrecorded in-place edit, second repo copy, pointer stub or rule file that repeats it. 5. Every path, script, tool and sibling skill it names still exists. Keep means it passes all five; merge means it has real content but fails test 3 or 4, so it folds into a named target; remove means it fails test 1 with nothing unique, or it is a copy, pointer, stray install or dead folder.
